subject: CobaltPay model trial & acceptance criteria — next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petro <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sam Turner <sam@cobaltpay.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: CobaltPay model trial & acceptance criteria — next steps

Thanks again for the demo time earlier — great to meet you and Andrea. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we have alignment on scope for the trial. TL;DR: we recommend a short open-model pilot (2–3 variants) run against your proprietary baseline with the prompt bundle attached, then evaluate using the benchmark CSV and acceptance thresholds below.

What we covered (summary)
- Core use case: transaction classification + downstream fraud-explain extraction for dispute triage.
- Volume profile: peak 600 req/s, median 120 req/s; SLO: p95 latency < 180ms for single-turn inference.
- Sensitive data: PII redaction required before storing outputs; CobaltPay wants retention=30 days for logs.

Proposed model candidates to trial (open options)
- Family A (optimized LLM-13B-int8): fast baseline, strong extraction accuracy on dev set.
- Family B (14B instruction-tuned): higher quality for few-shot extraction prompts, slightly higher latency.
- Family C (quantized 70B variant): for parity check vs your current proprietary model on hard extraction cases.

Acceptance thresholds we suggest for the pilot (we can adjust during prep)
- Core extraction exact-match: open-model within 3 percentage points absolute of proprietary baseline on the same test set.
- False positive rate (FP for fraud flagging): <= 2.0% absolute.
- Hallucination/unsupported assertions: measured as unsupported spans per 1k responses < 6.
- Latency: p95 < 180ms (infer on Redwood Dedicated config we propose) and cost per 1k tokens under target TBD with Sam.

Artifacts attached/links
- attached: prompt_bundle_v1.jsonl (sample prompts + canonical scoring harness)
- attached: cobaltpay_parity_benchmark.csv (labeled dev set + cutouts)
- Drive: openmodel_bench_report.pdf (example run notes + how we compute EM/RoUGE-L)
- bench runner repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-runner/tree/cobaltpay-trials

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Confirm you want us to run the 3-model pilot against 3k labeled examples (we can scale up). Reply with preferred start date (we can begin as soon as next Tue).
2) Share one security contact for the data ingestion scope (for retention/KMS conversation).
3) Andrea — please confirm the acceptance metrics above or suggest edits; Marissa/Rishi will scope infra and data work.

Best,
Olga Petro

Thanks, Olga — that recap is helpful and lines up with what Andrea and I discussed. A couple quick clarifications before we lock dates: 

1) Data retention: 30 days is acceptable for logs, but we need to keep raw request traces for 90 days within our environment for audit. Can Redwood support storing encrypted traces for 90 days in a customer-owned bucket?
2) Blind A/B: Andrea asked whether Redwood can run a blind A/B against our proprietary model (we'll provide a signed, tokenized interface). We want the evaluation to be double-blind if possible.
3) Start date: next Tue (2027-07-06) works on our side. We have a small pilot label team that can validate outputs over the first week.

Also tagging two internal stakeholders who will join later in the evaluation: 
- Priya N. (Product) — priya@cobaltpay.io
- Michael S. (Security) — michael@cobaltpay.io

Let us know what you need from us to schedule the run.

Sam

Appreciate the quick reply, Sam — answers inline below and a short execution plan.

1) Retention: Yes — we can support customer-owned encrypted traces in your S3/GCS bucket for 90 days. We'll surface an ingestion spec and an IaC snippet for your security team. Michael, we'll include KMS/HSM details in the follow-up packet.

2) Blind A/B: We can run a blind A/B. Recommended flow:
   - Redwood acts as the orchestrator; we proxy identical traffic to both models and store anonymized IDs.
   - Labeling team will be provided a blind sample export (no model labels) for human validation.
   - We provide pre-built analysis scripts (linked) that compute EM, ROUGE-L, and hallucination counts.

Suggested acceptance thresholds (refined for CobaltPay):
- Exact-match (EM) on extraction fields: open-model >= (prop_baseline - 3pp) on same holdout set.
- Failure mode taxonomy: we will measure hallucinations, missing-entities, and plausibility errors separately (acceptance if hallucinations per 1k < 6).
- Cost/latency tradeoff: if Family B matches EM and stays within 10% latency of your baseline, recommend promoting for canary at 5% production traffic.

Execution plan / timeline
- Thu (tomorrow): we share the ingestion spec + IaC for 90d traces; security packet for Michael.
- Mon 7/5: Redwood seeds bench runner with your 3k examples (we need a secure drop).
- Tue 7/6: Start pilot runs (3 model variants). Results shared by Fri 7/9 with candidate pick and recommended canary steps.

I've attached the prompt bundle and the CSV dev set to this thread. Rishi, can you confirm compute footprint & estimated token cost for the 3-model run (3k examples) so I can confirm to Sam?

Thanks,
Olga

Looping back internally with a quick plan and compute estimate. Quoting the key asks from the thread.

Plan (internal)
- Infra: We'll run the three variants on Redwood Dedicated (medium pool) with KV caching disabled for initial parity checks. Estimated GPU-time: ~6 GPU-hours total across the three models for 3k examples (batch size 8 typical).
- Token cost estimate: ~1.2M tokens total across the run; rough cost = $X (will provide exact once VM selection finalized).
- Eval: use the attached bench runner (linked above) to compute EM, ROUGE-L, hallucination counts. I'll run a dry pass tonight against 100 examples to sanity-check prompts.

Canary recommendation: promote winning open model to 5% traffic, monitor EM & hallucination metrics hourly for first 48 hours, rollback triggers = hallucination spike > 30% over baseline OR EM drop > 4pp.

Next internal step: Marissa, can you prep the labeler handoff notes for Sam's team? Olga, I'll send a calendar invite for Wed 7/7 to review run results and pick the canary candidate.
